title: Unique Length-3 Palindromic Subsequences
summary: Given a string, count the distinct length-three palindromic subsequences that can be derived from it, considering each distinct subsequence only once.
statement: Given a string, count the distinct length-three palindromic subsequences that can be derived from it, considering each distinct subsequence only once. A palindrome reads identically forward and backward, and a subsequence is formed by deleting some characters from the original string without altering the order of the remaining characters.
constraints: s has 3 through 100000 lowercase English letters.
Count distinct subsequence strings, not distinct index triples.
Every counted palindrome has the form x-y-x.
hints: Fixing the outer character reduces the question to which middle characters occur between its first and last positions.
Record the first and last position of each letter, then count distinct letters strictly between them.
For each alphabet letter with two occurrences, add the size of the set inside its widest span.
Any valid triple lies inside that widest span; conversely every distinct character inside it creates exactly one distinct palindrome for those ends.
editorial: Any valid triple lies inside that widest span; conversely every distinct character inside it creates exactly one distinct palindrome for those ends.

tests.explanation: The distinct palindromes are aaa, aba, and aca.
No character can serve as both ends of a length-three subsequence.
